conventions.convention: The normal points from the bounded interior into the connected exterior; both conormals use this same normal. Jumps are interior minus exterior.
The three-dimensional kernel is 1/(4π|x-y|), with minus its Laplacian equal to the source delta.

The fixed H1/2 Hilbert norm is the square sum of localized chart Fourier norms with weight (1+4π²|ξ|²)^(1/2), using the negative-sign 2π transform. Real H−1/2 is the continuous real dual; complex duality is linear in the density and conjugate-linear in the trace.

The homogeneous whole-space energy space is the gradient-norm completion of compactly supported smooth functions, realized in L6. Exterior finite-energy functions are also required to belong to L6, excluding arbitrary additive constants.
The double layer has trace jump −φ; W is minus its common conormal. Polyhedral edge and vertex assertions are Sobolev assertions, without pointwise half-jump coefficients there.

The Helmholtz branch separately assumes a connected C² obstacle boundary and connected exterior, k>0, real nonzero η, outgoing kernel exp(ikr)/(4πr), and combined potential Dk−iηSk. Bounds are at fixed frequency.
The two-dimensional kernel is −log|x-y|/(2π); dilation transports density by λs(sy)=λ(y)/s and retains total charge.

Assembly processes ordered panel pairs, charges physical source weights by 1/(4π), uses a cluster tail only when R>a+b, and reports a Sobolev form defect only with a verified positive lower coefficient-norm bound γh.

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. On the stated compact Lipschitz boundary, the interior and bounded exterior-collar H1 traces into H1/2 are bounded; there is a bounded compactly supported whole-space H1 right inverse, a bounded interior extension, and a bounded trace from the homogeneous gradient completion with its L6 realization.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Every real H−1/2 density has a unique homogeneous-energy weak single layer with common trace, conormal jump equal to its density, bounded trace map V:H−1/2→H1/2, and coercivity ⟨λ,Vλ⟩≥c‖λ‖². Bounded densities have the stated off-surface kernel representation.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Every H1/2 density has a unique minimum-energy transmission pair, harmonic on both sides, with trace jump −φ, common conormal, bounded energy, average trace and conormal maps, and the absolutely convergent off-surface double-layer kernel representation.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For the stated C² geometry, Sk:H−1/2→H1loc across the surface and Dk:H1/2→piecewise local H1 extend the classical layers boundedly, solve Helmholtz off the surface, have bounded weak conormals and Green identities, and satisfy the uniform outgoing Sommerfeld condition.

Under the stated choice and conforming-mesh assumptions, every Laplace P0 panel-pair integral is absolutely convergent and equals its weak V pairing. Touching pairs have finite smooth reference-triangle reductions with exponent zero; disjoint pairs have a smooth fallback. Certified algebraic geometry and refinable outward arithmetic give finite attainment of every positive absolute tolerance.
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Every exterior L6 function with local H1 regularity and square-integrable gradient has an H1/2 boundary trace bounded by its exterior gradient norm.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the stated C² geometry. A weak Helmholtz solution in H1 on every bounded exterior truncation, with zero obstacle trace and the uniform outgoing Sommerfeld condition, vanishes throughout the connected exterior.

The degree spaces are mutually orthogonal, their algebraic sum is uniformly dense in continuous sphere data, ordered projections converge in L2 for continuous data, smooth-data projections decay faster than every inverse power, and degree-ℓ evaluation and Cp norms have the stated polynomial bounds.

concerns.concern: Proof step 3.1 writes the arclength factor as “ds_Y=s,ds_y” rather than “ds_Y=s ds_y”. The following cancellation uses the intended multiplicative factor correctly.

Step 1.1 applies the capacity homothety theorem to S1 without checking its hypothesis 0<cap(S1)<∞. This is a short missing admissibility check: the logarithmic kernel is bounded below on the compact circle, while normalized arclength has finite energy because its diagonal singularity is logarithmically integrable.

seams_checked.note: The supplier proves reference-triangle vertex transformations and pure-coordinate Gaussian derivative bounds. The BEM panel-pair lemma separately derives touching-panel reductions, denominator bounds and nested errors before applying those results with exponent zero; it does not treat the supplier alone as a panel-pair certificate.

The actual single-cluster tail is used under R>a+b, with physical source charges vj/(4π), positive target-weight summation, and separate quadrature and arithmetic errors. Neither the algorithm nor transfer theorem imports a global three-dimensional tree complexity claim. Spherical harmonic normalization also agrees.

The BEM modal foundations use the exact positive-real spherical Bessel/Hankel definitions, radial equation, recurrence, Wronskian and outgoing asymptotics. They make no numerical stability or certified-evaluation claim from these symbolic identities.

The consumed supplier is lem-na-lipschitz-scalar-h1-h2-extension. Its bounded Lipschitz-domain H1 extension conclusion applies to the chart pieces and annuli used here; AC is retained. The BEM uses require neither its H2 conclusion nor vector-complex topology.

The graph-interface lemma uses thm-na-rademacher-euclidean for almost-everywhere differentiability of locally Lipschitz maps. Its open-domain hypotheses and AC assumption are preserved; no HJB scheme or viscosity conclusion is imported.

The exterior-wave page uses the relocated spherical problem, harmonic density/evaluation bounds, positive-real Hankel flux/nonvanishing and modewise outgoing expansion under their stated conventions. Its DtN and spherical uniqueness consumers supply their own convergence or boundary arguments; the general C² obstacle theorem is not substituted for a spherical model assumption.
